newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia rate policy favours investment - RBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia rate policy favours investment - RBA.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia said it saw a strong outlook for business investment, supported by relatively favourable financial conditions.
"Recent information, supports, if anything strengthens, the earlier picture that a very solid upswing in investment spending is underway," the Bank said in its quarterly econmic review.

"Monetary policy settings are supportive of investment," it said. "Nominal lending rates are low by historical standards and 'real' rates, as conventionally measured, are only slightly higher than they were in the second half of 1993, when policy settings were designed to help stimulate a weak economy."
The Bank said business investment would be led by a boom in non-residential construction.
It noted the value of private building approvals had risen to the peaks of the late 1980's property boom, thanks in part to a number of major projects related to the Olympics.
Engineering construction was already well above its peak in the late 1980s and as a share of Gross Domestic Product was close close to the high seen in the early 1980s.
"The positive investment outlook relatively optimistic expectations regarding the medium-term future of the Australian economy," the RBA said.
"Much of the investment is infrastructure related, or in the mining sector, and is not being undertaken solely in response to expected movements in the domestic business cycle," it said.
The RBA said it expected dwelling investment to soon augment the upswing in business invesmtnet, as evidence accumulates that the housing sector in the early stages of an upturn.
"Here again financial conditions are favourable for expansion," the central bank said.
The bank noted the predominant standard variable housing loan was at 8.25 percent, the lowest level since June 1974.
Since the report was prepared a number of banks have cut that rate further and it now stands at 7.55 percent.
